The present charge-sheet under Section 498A/306/34 IPC was committed to this Court on 14.08.2023 being a Sessions Triable Offence.

2. The case of the prosecution is as follows:
That on or before 04.05.2019 at House No. A-17, Gali No.2, Vijay Nagar, Mohan Garden, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi, the accused Rahul Kumar @ Sanjeet had instigated deceased Pooja to commit suicide and the deceased committed suicide on 04.05.2019 in between 02:00 am to 05:00 am.

It is further alleged that all the accused persons,
namely, Rahul Kumar @ Sanjeet, Janki Devi and Sita Devi subjected the deceased State vs Rahul Kumar@Sanjeet on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73167841/
1 Pooja to cruelty so as to instigate her to commit suicide.
As per the charge-sheet, the deceased Pooja got married to accused Rahul five years prior to the date of alleged incident.
It is alleged that accused persons used to regularly beat and torture the deceased.
On the complaint of the father of the deceased, the FIR was registered.
During the investigation of the case, postmortem of the deceased was conducted and FSL report was obtained.

On completion of investigation, it was concluded by the IO, that Accused Rahul Kumar @ Sanjeet had committed the offence punishable under Section 306 IPC and all accused persons had committed the offence punishable under Section 498A/34 IPC.

Final report under Section 173 Cr.P.C was put before Ld.
Metropolitan Magistrate with a view to put the accused persons on trial.

3. In the light of the police report and the documents filed along with the same, the Learned Metropolitan Magistrate having taken cognizance of the offence, complied with the provision of Section 207 Cr.P.C and committed the case to the Court of Session.

4. On 25.10.2023, after hearing the Additional Public Prosecutor for the State and the counsel for the Accused persons who conceded on charge, charges were framed against the Accused persons under Section 498A/34 IPC and against accused Rahul charge under Section 306 IPC was also framed.
The charge was read over to the accused persons, who pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

5. In support of the case, the prosecution got examined the following witnesses namely, PW-1 Dr.
Neeraj Kumar Garg, PW- 2 Paro Devi, PW-3 Shatrughan, PW-4 Ajit, PW-5 SI Satyawan, PW-6 Retired SI Dharambir Singh and PW-7 Sh. Puneet Kulshreshtha, Section Officer, LG Office.
6. On completion of Prosecution Evidence, the accused persons were examined under Section 313 Cr.P.C and their statements were recorded on 03.06.2024.

During their examination under Section 313 Cr.P.C, the accused persons denied having knowledge of the incrimination circumstances appearing in the evidence against them and stated that they had been falsely implicated in the present case.
7. At the stage of Defence evidence, accused persons did not wish to lead Defence Evidence.

10. PW-1

Dr. Neeraj Kumar Garg, CMO, CDMO Office, Sector - 2, Dwarka deposed that on 05.05.2019, he conducted postmortem of deceased Pooja, female, aged about 21 years and the detailed postmortem report was Ex.PW1/A.
He stated that the cause of death is asphyxia caused by ligature hanging by using chunni (dupatta like material) and the manner of death was suicide.

He stated that on receipt of FSL report, no poisonous substance was detected and time since death was State vs Rahul Kumar@Sanjeet on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73167841/

11. PW-2 Smt. Paro Devi deposed that deceased Pooja was her daughter and got married to accused Rahul @ Sanjeet five years prior to her death.
She stated that initially her daughter was residing in her matrimonial home and accused Janki Devi was her mother-in-law and Smt. Sita Devi was the sister-in-law of deceased daughter Pooja.
She stated that thereafter she shifted to Delhi and resided at House No. A-17, Gali No. 2, Vijay Nagar, Mohan Garden.
She stated that accused persons never demanded dowry nor gave beatings to her daughter Pooja.
She stated that on 04.05.2019, they came to know that her daughter was died as she was ill.

The witness was not cross-examined by counsel for all the accused persons.

SI Satyawan deposed that on 04.05.2019, on receipt of DD No. 26A, he alongwith Ct.
Umesh reached at H. No. A-17, Gali no. 2, Vijay Nagar, Mohan Garden, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi at about 07.00 AM where the dead body of the deceased lady was found on a bed and one chunni was found lying near the bed.
He added that accused Rahul Kumar @ Sanjeet was found at the spot alongwith Paro Devi, mother of deceased Pooja.

He stated that he called the crime team at the spot which came there and inspected and photographed the scene of crime and on inquiries, it was revealed that the deceased had died within seven years of her marriage.
He deposed that information was given to SDM Dwarka and the dead body of deceased was shifted to mortuary DDU Hospital, where the doctors declared her brought dead vide MLC no. 4232/19.

He stated that Smt.
Paro Devi and Sh. Shaturghan Das parents, Sh. Ajit, brother of deceased were produced before Executive Magistrate Sh. Puneet Kulshrestha in his office and he recorded their statements and directed to take action as per law.
He stated that he prepared rukka Ex.PW-5/A and got registered the present case and that during investigation, postmortem on the dead body of deceased was conducted.
He deposed that the chunni which was of light green and cream color was taken into possession at the spot and was sealed with the seal of SB vide seizure memo Ex.PW-5/B.
He stated that his request for post mortem examination was Ex.PW-5/C and he filled form 25/35, Ex.PW-5/D and the brief facts prepared by him were Ex.PW-5/E.

He further stated that he recorded the statements of Shaturghan Das and Ajit regarding the identification of dead body of deceased and after postmortem, the doctor handed over the viscera of deceased in a sealed pullanda with sample seal and he seized the same vide seizure memo Ex.PW-5/F.
He stated that the dead body was handed over to Sh. Shaturghan Das, father of deceased.

He further deposed that on 05.05.2019, accused Rahul was arrested by him vide arrest memo Ex.PW-5/G, his personal search was conducted vide memo Ex.PW-5/H and his disclosure statement was recorded, Ex.PW-5/H1.
He stated that during investigation, notices under Section 41 A Cr.P.C was served upon accused Sita Devi and Janki Devi and both these accused persons were interrogated.

He stated that notice served upon accused Sita Devi was Ex.PW-5/H2 and the notice served upon accused Janki Devi was Ex.PW-5/H3 and interrogation report of accused Sita Devi was Ex.PW-5/H4 and interrogation report of accused Janki Devi was Ex.PW-5/H5.
He stated that he deposited the case property in malkhana and during investigation, he had recorded statement of witnesses, collected relevant medical papers and send the exhibits to FSL.
He further stated that the report of FSL was collected and on his transfer, he handed over the case file to MHCR.

14.1 The said witness was cross-examined by counsel for all the accused persons wherein he stated that no suicide note was found and he did not make any inquiry from the neighbour with regard to any allegation of dispute or quarrel between the deceased and accused persons.

PW-6 Retired SI Dharambir Singh deposed that on 01.12.2020, the case file of the present case was assigned to him.

He deposed that he went through the case file and on perusal of the same, it was revealed that the investigation of the case was completed and accordingly, he prepared the charge-sheet and same was filed in the court through SHO and senior officials of police.
He deposed that after receipt of the FSL report, subsequent opinion Ex.PW6/A of the doctor was taken regarding the manner of death, which was opined to be suicidal.
15.1 The witness was not cross-examined by counsel for all the accused persons.

Sh. Puneet Kulshresth, Section Officer, LG Secretariat, deposed that on 04.05.2019, he was posted at Tehsildar - cum- Executive Magistrate, Dwarka and information was received in the Office of SDM, Dwarka regarding death of deceased within seven years of marriage.
He stated that he was directed by the SDM to conduct inquest and he recorded the statements of Paro Devi, Shatrughan Dass and Ajit who were the family members of deceased Pooja.

He stated that police was directed to conduct postmortem of deceased Pooja and his request for postmortem examination was Ex.PW7/A. 16.1 During his cross-examination by counsel for all the accused persons
, he denied that Paro Devi, Shatrughan Das and Ajit were tutored by Police for giving the specific statement before being produced in his office.

17. On 08.02.2024, the accused persons admitted the following documents under Section 294 Cr.P.C., namely, FIR No. 281/19 Ex.A1, endorsement on rukka Ex.A2, certificate under Section 65B of The Indian Evidence Act Ex.A3, DD No. 26A Ex.A4, FSL report Ex.A5, MLC of Pooja Ex.A6 and Crime Team Report Ex.A7.
18.

None of the material witnesses examined by the prosecution in the present case, namely,
mother, father and brother of the deceased, PW-2, PW-3 and PW-4 have stated that the deceased was subjected to dowry or was harassed and abused by the accused persons as alleged.

Further,
there is no evidence on record to even prima facie suggest that the accused persons had committed the offence of dowry death or had harassed the victim so as to instigate or abet her suicide by hanging.

It has also not been proved during trial that the accused Rahul had allegedly committed the offence of abetment of suicide as none of the witnesses examined have deposed of any ill-treatment or abuse or any harassment inflicted on deceased Pooja immediately prior to her death.
It is significant to mention that IO during his cross-examination has stated that he had come to know that the allegations made by the family of the deceased were not confirmed by the neighbours.
No other eye witness or material witness has been cited or examined to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
19. The complicity of the accused persons could have been proved by the ocular evidence or circumstantial evidence.
The material witnesses who are the mother, father and brother of the deceased turned hostile and the circumstantial evidence is insufficient to infer the guilt of accused persons.
It is well settled law that to convict the accused persons on circumstantial evidence there must be complete chain of events pointing towards the guilt of the accused persons and no other.

It was held by the Hon'ble Apex court in Hanumant Govind Nargundkar and Anr. V. State of Madhya Pradesh, AIR 1952 SC 343, that:

entities.text: Hanumant Govind Nargundkar and Anr. V. State of Madhya Pradesh, AIR 1952 SC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"It is well to remember that in cases where the evidence is of a circumstantial nature,
the circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is to be drawn should be in the first instance be fully established and all the facts so established should be consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused.
Again, the circumstances should be of a conclusive nature and tendency and they should be such as to exclude every hypothesis but the one proposed to be proved.

In other words, there must be a chain of evidence so far complete as not to leave any reasonable ground for a conclusion consistent with the innocence of the accused and it must be such as to show that within all human probability the act must have been done by the accused."

20. In case of Sharad Birdhi Chand Sharda Vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1984 SC 1622, the Hon'ble Apex Court had laid down the test which are pre-requisites before conviction should be recorded,
which are as under:
(1) The circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is to be drawn should be fully established; (2) The circumstances concerned "must or should" and not "may be" established; (3) The facts so established should be consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, State Vs. Mohd. Khalil FIR No. 148/2017, PS Chandni Mahal 9 of 11 that is to say, they should not be explainable on any other hypothesis except that the accused is guilty; (4) The circumstances should be of conclusive nature and tendency; (5) They should exclude every possible hypothesis except the one to be proved; and (6) There must be a chain of evidence so complete as not to leave any reasonable ground for conclusion consistent with the innocence of the accused and must so that in all human probability the act must have been done by the accused.
21.

sentences.text: It is well settled law that the burden to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt lies on the shoulder of the prosecution.
The accused has a right to maintain silence in the trial.
Every accused is to be presumed innocent until proved guilty.
The burden of proof on the prosecution is to prove the case by leading cogent, convincing and reliable evidence so as to prove the guilt of accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused persons cannot be convicted on the basis of mere probabilities or presumptions.
Suspicion howsoever grave cannot take place of proof.

22. In the present case, the main star witnesses, namely, Paro Devi, Shatrughan Das and Ajit who are the parents and brother of the deceased respectively have turned hostile and there is no other witness to prove the complicity of the accused persons in the commission of the present offence.
The circumstantial evidence is insufficient and does not form complete chain of events leading to the inescapable conclusion of guilt of accused persons.
23. Thus, this Court unflinchingly holds that the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the accused persons by leading convincing or cogent evidence.
The prosecution has failed to discharge the burden placed upon it and therefore, the accused persons are entitled to be exonerated.
